answer: Each agent must post a bonded container slot whose unique sonnet-derived yard coordinate is verified against the terminal's stack plan before any move is scheduled. A mirror stack audits every claimed identity against the yard's rehandling ledger, so duplicate slots collide and get flagged at the inlet gate before crane allocation. Attacker cost scales with reserved stack space and forfeited bonds per fake slot, but collusion that buys real distinct slots still passes, capping this at resource-priced resistance.
